back: A controller repeatedly observes actual state, compares it with the desired state stored in the API, and acts to close the gap. It is level-triggered, so it converges even after missing events.

front: What does kube-apiserver do with every request?
back: Authentication → authorization (RBAC) → mutating admission → schema validation → validating admission → persist to etcd. It also serves watches. It is the only component that talks to etcd.

front: What is etcd and how many members should it have?
back: A Raft-based, strongly consistent key-value store holding all cluster state. Use an odd number (3 or 5) so a majority quorum survives failures; back it up.
Watches pods with no `spec.nodeName`, filters out nodes that cannot run them, scores the rest, and writes a Binding. It never starts containers.
One binary running the built-in controllers (Deployment, ReplicaSet, Job, Node, EndpointSlice, garbage collector, ...). Only one instance is active at a time via Lease-based leader election.
Runs on each node, watches pods bound to it, starts them through the CRI, runs probes, mounts volumes, reports status and heartbeats. It also runs static pods from `/etc/kubernetes/manifests`.
The Container Runtime Interface: a gRPC API the kubelet uses to talk to runtimes like containerd or CRI-O, which use an OCI runtime (runc) to create containers.
Watches Services and EndpointSlices and programs kernel rules (iptables or nftables) on each node so Service virtual IPs load-balance to pod IPs.

front: Name the chain of objects and controllers behind a Deployment.
back: Deployment → (Deployment controller) → ReplicaSet → (ReplicaSet controller) → Pods → (scheduler binds) → kubelet runs containers via CRI.
`spec` is desired state written by you; `status` is observed state written by controllers. Never put `status` in your manifests.
`metadata.generation` increments on spec changes; the controller copies it to `status.observedGeneration` after reconciling. A lag means it has not caught up.
Labels identify and are used by selectors (short values, max 63 chars). Annotations hold non-identifying metadata for tools and humans and are never used for selection.
A pod defined by a manifest file on a node and run directly by the kubelet, without the scheduler. The API shows a read-only mirror pod. kubeadm and kind run the control plane this way.

front: Three ways to explore the API from the CLI
back: `kubectl api-resources` / `api-versions` (discovery), `kubectl explain <path>` (schema), `kubectl get --raw /path` or `kubectl proxy` + curl (raw HTTP). Add `-v=6` to see requests.
They link a child to its owner (Pod → ReplicaSet → Deployment). The garbage collector uses them for cascading deletion of children when the owner is deleted.
